# The Magisterial deck

**What it rewards:** Playing the draft. Its strength comes from combinations of cards the player finds while drafting, from boons paid on draft, and from culture, great people of every family, great-person works and wonders. A single card is modest; the right set of abilities together is strong. **Directions inside it:** a reroll and pass engine; a deep collection beyond the chairs; boons and random gifts; culture converted into whatever the empire lacks; great-person works arranged to claim land; wonders that pay across the empire.

*Initially generated by `scripts/deckDocs.mjs`; now a hand-edited design spec (deck-list pass, 2026-10-06).*

- **built**: exists in the game as written.
- **revised**: exists, and this sheet changes it; the last column says what it was.
- **new**: proposed on this sheet; the last column says whether an existing effect shape fits or what new mechanic it needs.
- **deferred**: in the data but not dealt; the note says why.
- **cut**: listed only under Proposed cuts.

**Words this sheet uses.**
- A **hand** is a draft offer. **Drafting** takes a card from it. **Passing** gives the whole hand up. **Rerolling** pays to have it dealt again. **Seating** puts a card you hold into a chair; **unseating** takes it out.
- A **reward hand** is a free Order hand dealt by an event or a card, outside the culture meter.
- Your **collection** is every Order you hold, seated or not.
- **On draft** means the card pays once, when you take it. Some boon cards do nothing while seated; they still count toward cards that read your collection.
- A **commission** is a goal card: seat it, reach the goal, take the reward, and it leaves its chair. Commissions pay no beads.

**Draft-action families.** Each draft action has cards that let you take it more often or more cheaply, and cards that pay you each time you take it. None of them names another card.
- **Reroll.** Enablers: The Second Reading (the first reroll of each hand is free), The Salon des Refusés (reroll with culture). Payers: The Critics' Circle, Commission: The Salon Season. Faith from Devotion and gold from Commerce's The Brokers' Redraw also pay for rerolls.
- **Pass.** Enablers: The Patient Eye (a pass refunds culture), The Archive (keep one card from a passed hand). Payers: The Unwritten Chapter, The Book of Refusals, The Return of the Exiles, Commission: The Salon Season.
- **Draft.** Enablers: The Open Door (hands cost less), Officials by Merit (larger hands), The Talent Scouts (larger great-person hands), The Subscription List (gold into the draft pool), and every reward-hand card. Payers: The Accessions Register (a charter counts), and every boon card.
- **Seat and unseat.** Enablers: The Rotating Chairs (shorter seals), The Antechamber (an extra chair). Payers: The Swearing-In, and The Senate Charter's Assembly Hall (pays per filled wildcard chair).
- **Reward hands.** Sources: The Unveiling (wonders), The New Code (captures), The Grand Lottery, and the commissions. They are drafts, so the draft payers read them.
- **The collection.** Pure boon cards (Gifts at Court, The Welcome Feast, The Wandering Muse, The Grand Lottery, The Cabinet of Curiosities) and The Archive grow the collection without taking a chair. The Encyclopedia, The Universal Library and Commission: The Full Council read it.

## What stands

Counts cover the cards exclusive to Magisterial; shared cards are listed separately. Cut cards are not counted.

| Tier | Cards | Built | Revised | New | Deferred |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tier 0 | 14 | 7 | 1 | 5 | 1 |
| Tier I | 25 | 12 | 1 | 9 | 3 |
| Tier II | 27 | 7 | 2 | 15 | 3 |
| Tier III | 21 | 5 | 4 | 11 | 1 |
| Tier IV | 4 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 2 |
| **All** | **91** | **31** | **8** | **42** | **10** |

Deep enough for eleven chairs: 87 exclusive cards and 12 shared ones are available by Tier III, and Magisterial's own chair cards (The Antechamber, Commission: The Wonder of the Age) only add to the demand a little.

### How the shelf is weighted

| Tier | Common | Uncommon | Rare |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tier 0 | 10 | 3 | 1 |
| Tier I | 8 | 14 | 3 |
| Tier II | 6 | 15 | 6 |
| Tier III | 3 | 11 | 7 |
| Tier IV | 0 | 1 | 3 |

## Synergies with other decks

### Dominion: the triumph
- **What each gives.** Dominion gives great generals and citadels, which Magisterial's any-family cards pay on like any other work, and captured cities full of buildings and wonders. Magisterial gives boons that fill an army's gaps (a random great person, production on draft), culture turned into production, and wonders that pay across the empire.
- **Hooks Magisterial creates:** great-person works of any family, wonders, reward hands. **Hooks it reads from Dominion:** captured cities (The New Code, The Looted Gallery, Triumphal Arches), citadels (every card that pays on a great-person work), garrisons (The Imperial Examinations, Examinations of State).
- **Shared improvements:** citadels. A citadel counts toward The Four-Part Garden and Commission: The Patron's Gallery like any other work.
- **Cards on this sheet that serve the pair:** The New Code, The Looted Gallery, Gifts at Court, The Wandering Muse, The Working Court, The Groundskeepers, The Laureate, The Masters' Domain, The Patron's Gallery (commission); shared: Triumphal Arches, The Imperial Examinations, Examinations of State.

### Expansionist: shaping territory
- **What each gives.** Expansionist gives room: claimed and tended land to place works on, in the patterns Magisterial's arrangement cards reward. Magisterial gives culture (Expansionist's gap) and territory: works that claim the land around them.
- **Hooks Magisterial creates:** great-person works that claim land (The Landmark Bounds, The Four-Part Garden, Commission: The Paradise Garden). **Hooks it reads from Expansionist:** tended tiles, which count as sides of a four-part garden; works placed side by side on claimed land (The Quarter of Masters); farms and forests and hills beside works (The Sculpted Landscape, The Siting Masters).
- **Shared improvements:** manufactories (paid on by every any-family work card), and landmarks beside tended land.
- **Cards on this sheet that serve the pair:** The Landmark Bounds, The Siting Masters, The Quarter of Masters (taken from the Expansionist sheet), The Four-Part Garden, Commission: The Paradise Garden, The Groundskeepers; shared: The Sculpted Landscape, Garden Provinces, Garden Cities. The landscape-garden idea (tended land that pays culture) belongs on the Expansionist sheet; this sheet leaves it there.

### Commerce: the art market
- **What each gives.** Commerce gives gold that buys draft actions, and merchants and customs houses for the any-family cards. Magisterial gives culture turned into gold, and boons that save purchases.
- **Hooks Magisterial creates:** draft actions that can be bought (The Subscription List pays gold into the draft pool; The Brokers' Redraw's gold rerolls feed The Critics' Circle and Commission: The Salon Season). **Hooks it reads from Commerce:** gold and purchases (Public Benefactors, The Great Patrons and The Artisan Court's cheaper culture buildings), foreign routes (Travelling Players, The Cosmopolitan Court, The Patrons' Road).
- **Shared improvements:** customs houses, and landmarks on trade routes (The Cosmopolitan Court pays gold on works).
- **Cards on this sheet that serve the pair:** The Subscription List, The Grand Fairs, The Patrons' Road, Public Benefactors, The Performers' Treasury, The Universal Court, The Critics' Circle; shared: Travelling Players, The Cosmopolitan Court.

### Devotion: the cathedral
- **What each gives.** Devotion gives faith, which is what rerolls cost today, so a Devotion empire is the natural engine for the reroll family; and holy sites. Magisterial gives wonders, culture, and boons that include faith.
- **Hooks Magisterial creates:** wonders and great-person works; faith from culture buildings (The Temple of the Muses) and faith on draft (The Grand Lottery). **Hooks it reads from Devotion:** faith spent on rerolls (The Critics' Circle), holy sites (Sacred Commissions), Cathedrals (The Magister's Court).
- **Shared improvements:** holy sites and landmarks.
- **Cards on this sheet that serve the pair:** The Rising Nave, The Temple of the Muses, The Civic Pantheon, The Grand Lottery, The Second Reading, The Critics' Circle, The Magister's Court; shared: Sacred Commissions, Sacred Patronage.

### Scientific: the academy
- **What each gives.** Scientific gives charters, which are drafted and so count as drafts, and scholars and academies for the any-family cards. Magisterial gives more drafts and rerolls, so Scientific sees more charters and can reroll for the one it needs.
- **Hooks Magisterial creates:** rerolls and extra choice in a draft (The Second Reading, The Open Door, Officials by Merit, The Antechamber). **Hooks it reads from Scientific:** charters as drafts (The Accessions Register), academies (The Museum Quarter, The House of Wisdom), libraries (Illuminated Treatises).
- **Shared improvements:** academies and landmarks (The Museum Quarter pays when they stand together).
- **Cards on this sheet that serve the pair:** Officials by Merit, The Encyclopedia, The Museum Quarter, The Accessions Register, The Learned Patron, The Senate Charter; shared: The House of Wisdom, Illuminated Treatises.
